verdicts.trueWording: reads like the retelling of a tale first told centuries ago
verdicts.note: Guardian style-and-voice paragraph. Quote verbatim. The 'cumulative effect of restraint' limb holds: the sentence opens 'Consequently,' directly after the catalogue of restraint (scarce metaphors, sparing dialogue, frugal description, no wisecracks, no tricks), and the clause about twists handed down through generations of storytellers follows in the same sentence. ACCESS FLAG for the eight Guardian rows (420-427): theguardian.com/robots.txt names anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User in its blocked list, and its header asserts content may not be used for LLM purposes. No Wayback capture of this URL exists (availability API returns no snapshot), so the raw page was reached only via recovery route 1, a browser user agent on the live URL. The verification is sound, but whether these eight rows may be KEPT and quoted downstream is a licensing call for the owner, not the lane.

verdicts.trueWording: Such specificity is persuasive because it sounds too detailed
verdicts.note: Guardian, paragraph after the blockquote from the novel. Quote verbatim; page continues 'to be made up.' Both limbs hold: the preceding block quotation is a passage from the novel in which a girl bobs her head and hides her eyes with her hands to show respect, as women did in the East Reach.

verdicts.trueWording: a studied neutrality of style tastes like clingfilm
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim, but the enumeration limb fails. The page names THREE hazards in one sentence, separated by semicolons: the cod-historic narratorial voice, jarring neologisms ('totally awesome'), and then studied neutrality. It never frames these as two failure modes, nor pairs neutrality against the cod-historic voice as its opposite. The 'Scylla and Charybdis' figure two sentences earlier applies to style and voice generally, not to this list.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that studied neutrality is one of only TWO failure modes, the other being the cod-historic voice - the page names a third, jarring neologisms, between them

verdicts.trueWording: feels like being locked inside a medieval theme park
verdicts.note: Guardian style-and-voice paragraph. The claim's quote fragment 'A cod-historic narratorial voice in a fantasy novel' and the theme-park predicate are contiguous and verbatim on the page. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: rich enough to nourish the reader's imagination, but frugal enough
verdicts.note: Guardian style-and-voice paragraph; page continues 'to allow it to collaborate in the act of creation.' Quote verbatim. The 'in A Wizard of Earthsea' limb is contextual rather than explicit - the sentence reads 'Descriptions of people and places are...' inside the paragraph that quotes the novel and concludes about A Wizard of Earthsea - but the antecedent is unambiguous.

verdicts.trueWording: thumbnail sketches contain the psychological depth of oil paintings
verdicts.note: Guardian, Pechvarry paragraph. Quote verbatim. The 'appear only briefly' limb is directly supported: the same paragraph says the other characters are minor in terms of screen time and that even the characters that appear most fleetingly are endowed with a fully thought-out inner life.

verdicts.trueWording: trade-routes, local politics, class hierarchies, infant mortality, abuse, addiction and slavery
verdicts.note: Guardian, paragraph beginning 'Earthsea is a fantasy world' - the locator in the claim is correct. The seven-item list is verbatim and in order. One softening to note: the page reads 'so human a world - with [list] - that its fantastical elements feel ALMOST quotidian'; the claim drops 'almost'. The hedge is minor and the substance holds, so this is not downgraded, but downstream copy should keep 'almost'.

verdicts.trueWording: moments of foreshadowing and authorial omniscience but no tricks
verdicts.note: Guardian style-and-voice paragraph. Page reads 'There are moments of foreshadowing and authorial omniscience but no tricks.' Quote verbatim; the subject is A Wizard of Earthsea, named in the immediately following sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: her graceful prose, carefully thought-through premises, psychological insight
verdicts.note: NYRB, paragraph beginning 'Which brings us to Ursula K. Le Guin' - locator correct. Quote verbatim. The 'first among the qualities' limb holds literally: graceful prose heads the list, and the list's verb is 'have earned her the National Book Award, the Kafka Award, five Hugos, five Nebulas...'. Byline Margaret Atwood confirmed in the page title.

verdicts.trueWording: non-directive understanding and recording are the functions required
verdicts.note: NYRB, paragraph setting out the Ekumen premise. Quoted fragment is contiguous and verbatim. All limbs hold: the sentence names a benevolent federation called the Ekumen whose explorers or ambassadors are known as Mobiles, sent to societies to see what has become of them. Orthography note only - the page writes 'noninvasive' unhyphenated where the claim paraphrases 'non-invasive'; that word is outside the quoted span.

verdicts.trueWording: at times a movingly lyrical writer
verdicts.note: NYRB, paragraph on 'Old Music and the Slave Women' - locator correct. Page reads that Le Guin, although at times a movingly lyrical writer, has never shied away from necessary gore. Quote verbatim; 'never avoided writing gore when the story required it' is an accurate rendering of 'never shied away from necessary gore'.

verdicts.trueWording: beguiled by the flawless, poetic prose
verdicts.note: Kirkus review of TEHANU / THE LAST BOOK OF EARTHSEA by Ursula K. Le Guin; no byline on the page, so 'unsigned' holds. Quote verbatim, page reading 'but even young readers will be beguiled by the flawless, poetic prose'. Metadata correction for the citation, not a claim limb: the page dates the review to Kirkus Reviews Issue Jan. 15, 1990; Feb. 1, 1990 is the book's release date.

verdicts.trueWording: a tale with the universality and dignity of legend
verdicts.note: Same Kirkus review. Page reads 'She weaves contemporary concerns - the roles of men and women, the theft of resources from and the passage of power to the next generation - into a tale with the universality and dignity of legend.' Quote verbatim; the subject 'She' is Le Guin, named in the preceding sentence. Same Jan. 15, 1990 issue-date correction as index 433.

verdicts.trueWording: her sentences, as elegant and beautiful as any written
verdicts.note: Library of America tribute, Zadie Smith entry (first entry under her heading). Page continues 'in the twentieth century.' Quote verbatim and attribution confirmed. Metadata note only: the page's dateline now reads January 5, 2022, a CMS re-date - the text itself places the writing days after Le Guin's death on January 22, 2018.

Library of America tribute, Harold Bloom entry. Quote verbatim; page continues 'Every word was exactly in place and every sentence or line had resonance.' Attribution confirmed under the Harold Bloom heading. Same January 5, 2022 CMS dateline note as index 437.
